newsitem.title: CHINA: Siemens plans to double China investment.
newsitem.headline: Siemens plans to double China investment.

text.p: German industrial giant Siemens AG is planning to double its investment in China to more than $800 million by 2001, the China Daily newspaper said on Saturday.

Siemens' business volume in China was seen accounting for more than half the company's total sales in the Asia-Pacific region, the newspaper quoted Hermann Koelle, president of Siemens China, as saying.
The company now had a total investment in China of $408 million, it quoted Koelle as saying.

Siemens was planning one joint venture in Zhuzhou in the southern province of Hunan to build locomotives for high-speed trains and another in southwestern Sichuan province's Deyang to make generating units for coal-fired power plants, Koelle said.
The firm was also expected to have a role in electrifying a railway between the northeastern cities of Harbin and Dalian, the newspaper said but gave no further details.
